Case report

extractions.quote:
She showed lumbar hyperlordosis, increased axial and lower limb muscle tone, spontaneous or action-induced painful spasms and the presence of head retraction reflex. Lower limb deep tendon reflexes were brisk. Extensor plantar reflex was present bilaterally.
Electromyography of paraspinal, abdominal and leg muscles showed continuous motor unit activity at rest.
She was diagnosed with SPS and was treated with pregabalin (150 mg twice a day) with a marked reduction of the body stiffness and the recovery of ambulation from the first days of treatment.

Detection of anti-neuronal antibodies was performed in the laboratory of the hospital (ISO 9001 certified). Over the years these episodes had been interpreted as psychiatric or epileptic; she had been treated with buxamine/phenobarbital/phenitoine at a dosage of 500/100/100 mg/day, clonazepam at a daily dose of 6 mg, diazepam at a dose of 15 mg/day, levetiracetam up to 3000 mg/day, valproate at a dose of 1000 mg/day and lacosamide up to 200 mg/day, without improvement.
